verdict.headline: Nvidia earnings beat sends chip sector higher; durable goods beats, Warsh keynote Friday
verdict.label: ES +0.35%; NQ +0.66%; NVDA $225 pre-mkt (+7.3%); durable goods July +1.1% vs 0.4% expected; AMD $475 pre-mkt (-0.92%); BTC $77,992; Marvell earns tonight; Warsh keynote Fri 10 AM ET
verdict.rationale_short: NVDA's dual-bar beat enters the regular session as a $225 pre-market print — up 7.3% from Wednesday's $210 close — while July durable goods +1.1% (vs. +0.4% consensus) adds a second constructive macro signal. AMD's -0.92% pre-market divergence is the first sign the market may be treating NVDA's beat as Blackwell-specific demand rather than sector-wide. Tonight's Marvell print (Q2 FY27; $12.2B Google custom chip deal) will either confirm sector breadth or narrow it to NVDA. The week's defining event — Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote at 10 AM ET Friday — arrives with chip-sector multiples at their most expanded point of the cycle. If the 30Y crosses 5.25% before Friday close, this read no longer holds.

watchlist_mentions.note: $225.21 pre-market (+7.3% from $210 regular close). Dual-bar beat confirmed: Q3 guide $108B (vs. $104.2B consensus) excludes China DC entirely; FY28 guidance 70% revenue growth; Vera CPU revenue more than doubles. AWS 2M GPU + millions of Vera CPU commitment through 2027-28. Watch whether two consecutive regular-session closes above $220 materialize — AH and pre-market momentum vs institutional confirmation.

$474.76 pre-market (-0.92% from $479.18 close). Unusual divergence from NVDA's +7.3% — the market is pricing Blackwell-specific demand rather than sector-wide read-through. Raymond James Strong Buy ($641 target), NVDA dual-bar beat, and durable goods all argue for the $484 ceiling breaking. Pre-market move says it hasn't happened yet. Two consecutive regular-session closes above $484 on above-average volume remain the confirmation signal; fade below $460 Thursday would signal institutional skepticism of the sector read-through.

~$496 (prior close). 10Y at 4.64% is a meaningful long-duration benefit to Azure's run rate. Durable goods beating supports enterprise demand. Canada tariff margin headwind unchanged; effective September 8.

trade_setups.thesis: NVDA pre-market at $225.21 reflects AH and overnight momentum on the dual-bar beat. The structural question for Thursday's regular session: whether institutional accumulation confirms the move or whether AH momentum meets distribution. CSCO and AMAT both ran into AH fades after clean beats this cycle. NVDA's +7.3% pre-market is more constructive than those cases, but the pattern warrants watching regular-session volume at $220.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive regular-session closes above $220 on above-average volume would signal institutional confirmation, distinguishing momentum from distribution. A fade back below $215 Thursday with declining volume on the gap fill would be the distribution signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh hawkish keynote Friday pushing the 30Y above 5.25% would add rate compression to an expanded multiple simultaneously. If 30Y crosses 5.25%, this setup's favorable asymmetry inverts.
trade_setups.horizon: Thursday through Friday close; Warsh keynote is the gating event.

trade_setups.thesis: AMD pre-market -0.92% to $474.76 despite NVDA's dual-bar beat and Raymond James's Strong Buy upgrade. The ceiling at $484 has now held across fourteen consecutive sessions, including the first post-NVDA-beat session. The pre-market divergence signals the market is pricing AMD's thesis as dependent on something beyond NVDA's Blackwell confirmation — possibly AMD's own Q3 results, server CPU competition with Intel, or a specific catalyst that the demand confirmation alone doesn't deliver.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive regular-session closes above $484 on above-average volume confirm the ceiling has broken. A regular-session open below $480 with a fade toward $470 signals the NVDA beat is being treated as Blackwell-specific, not a sector-wide read-through.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh hawkish Friday keynote pushing 30Y above 5.25% adds rate compression to the AMD multiple and extends the ceiling's hold regardless of the demand backdrop.
trade_setups.horizon: Thursday regular session through Friday close.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y Treasury / Rate Regime — Warsh keynote 24 hours out
trade_setups.thesis: 30Y at 5.15% — 15bps below the 5.30% regime trigger — with Warsh's first keynote as Fed Chair arriving Friday at 10 AM ET. September hike odds at ~33%, meaning a neutral-to-hold framing is approximately priced. The backdrop entering the speech is the most constructive since late 2025: PCE core 3.3% in-line, durable goods +1.1%, NVDA's demand cycle confirmed. The asymmetry is skewed hawkish: dovish pushes 30Y toward 5.05-5.10%, formally deactivating the regime threshold; a hawkish framing citing headline PCE at 3.7% and Canada tariff cost-push (effective September 8) would push 30Y back above 5.20-5.25%.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y holding below 5.20% through Friday close would formally deactivate the rate-regime risk for the first time since mid-July. A sustained break above 5.25% following the keynote re-triggers compression concerns heading into September FOMC.
trade_setups.invalidation: If Bessent names a Chinese bank before Warsh speaks Friday, an oil spike toward $89-91 hands the Fed Chair a simultaneous commodity-inflation signal that would increase the probability of a hawkish framing.

bear_case: NVDA's $225 pre-market prices two assumptions simultaneously: that the Q3 $108B guide is a conservative floor (China export licensing eases or Huawei Ascend share gain slows) and that gross margin stabilizes above 74.9% despite rising memory and wafer costs. At 24x+ forward revenue — the most expensive multiple this cycle — margin compression from either direction meets the largest multiple expansion the tape has seen. AMD's -0.92% pre-market despite NVDA's +7.3% is the market's first vote that the beat may be Blackwell-specific; if Marvell misses tonight, that differentiation hardens. Warsh's Friday keynote arrives 24 hours after the chip sector's maximum expansion moment; a hawkish framing citing Canada tariff cost-push and 3.7% headline PCE pushes the 10Y above 4.70% into a window where multiples have just been re-rated upward. If the 30Y crosses 5.25% before Friday close, this read no longer holds.
